content:
- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (sentiment > 0.10) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (sentiment < 0.0) — model is overly conservative, missing upward momentum.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays reacting to recent sentiment shifts, especially when sentiment turns positive after a dip.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects downward after strong upward moves, failing to capture sustained momentum.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile — adjust downward by 1–2% for first 7 days.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3+ days, model should not overreact to short-term volatility — cap upward revisions at +3% above recent 7-day average.
